- Appearance & General Behaviour: Not recorded (telehealth). Patient described by GP as “quite distressed.”

- Emergency Contact: Not recorded

Formulation
The patient presents with new-onset anxiety symptoms over the past ~2 months, temporally associated with starting a stressful new job and difficulties with a manager (precipitating factors). Family history of maternal depression may predispose to mood/anxiety vulnerability. Symptoms include significant anticipatory anxiety, palpitations, insomnia, low mood, anhedonia, social withdrawal, and reduced activity, which perpetuate functional impairment and distress. Alcohol intake on weekends may exacerbate sleep and anxiety. Protective factors include strong family support, insight, and willingness to engage in therapy. Palpitations are likely anxiety-related but basic medical evaluation is planned to exclude contributing causes.

Mental Health Care Plan Details
(Address each principal problem identified in Clinical Assessment - Section A. Add additional problems as relevant.)

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Reduce daily anxiety related to work and morning dread
  - Feel more able to attend work and function without constant worry
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Initiate evidence-based talking therapy (e.g., CBT via NHS pathway)
  - Provide self-help/online resources for anxiety management
  - Monitor symptoms and functioning; consider medication if insufficient response
- Actions (Patient):
  - Self-refer to NHS talking therapy service using link provided by GP
  - Engage with online anxiety resources provided
  - Contact GP if anxiety worsens or interferes with ability to work/cope
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provide self-referral link for talking therapy
  - Share online anxiety management resources
  - Safety-net: advise patient to call back if symptoms worsen or functioning declines
  - Consider pharmacotherapy if inadequate response to therapy/self-help

Secondary Problem (if applicable):
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Improve sleep duration and quality
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Implement sleep hygiene strategies and monitor response
- Actions (Patient):
  - Follow sleep guidance provided by GP
  - Monitor sleep patterns and triggers (e.g., late-night worry, alcohol)
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provide written advice on sleep hygiene and strategies to improve sleep

Tertiary Problem:
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Understand and reduce palpitations
  - Exclude medical contributors
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Conduct basic blood tests to rule out physiological causes
  - Review results and correlate with anxiety symptoms
- Actions (Patient):
  - Call support line to arrange blood tests
  - Attend GP follow-up one week after tests are completed
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Order basic blood tests (specific tests not documented)
  - Arrange/confirm follow-up appointment to review results and plan

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Anxiety and therapy options (talking therapy/CBT), online self-help resources, sleep hygiene strategies, plan to obtain blood tests, when to seek further help
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening:
  - Inability to cope with work or daily tasks
  - Escalating anxiety/panic symptoms
  - Further deterioration in sleep or significant functional decline
- Coping Strategies:
  - Use online resources and techniques provided
  - Engage with talking therapy once arranged
  - Utilize family support
  - Follow sleep hygiene advice

Consent, Coordination & Review
- Patient Consent to Plan: Yes (agreed to therapy referral and investigations)
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: Planned self-referral to NHS talking therapy service (service name not recorded)
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not recorded
- Review Date: GP follow-up planned one week after blood tests are completed (exact date not recorded)

Quality checks:
● Missing but clinically expected elements: Formal diagnosis; standardized screening scores (e.g., GAD-7, PHQ-9); comprehensive MSE and cognitive assessment; medications/allergies/PMH; quantified alcohol use; explicit overall risk level; emergency contact; specific blood tests listed; concrete review date.
● Internal conflicts from the transcript: Chest pain—patient initially denies chest pain, then describes pain when heart is beating fast (conflict noted). Palpitations described as irregular; no medical confirmation documented.
● Transcript quality notes: Some sections unclear/elliptical; telehealth format; no objective measures or screening tools documented; no medication/allergy history obtained.
